correctness.rationale: The original geodesic criterion follows from the two intermediates of every length-2 coordinate square and induction on Hamming distance. Distance-two exclusion decomposes by parity and maximality is independent domination. Each halfcube has 64 vertices and closed neighborhoods of size 22; pair overlaps are 6 for distance 4 and 0 for distance 6. No three centers dominate, using a pair at distance 4. Four independent centers have r=0,1,2 disjoint distance-six pairs, giving union at most 56, exactly 60, or exactly 64 respectively. At r=2 complementary-coordinate supports force an affine plane with differences of weights 4,4,6. Counting 224 distance-six pairs times 10 complements divided by two gives exactly 1120 minimal configurations per parity class. Squaring gives 1254400. An independent finite enumerator finds exactly the same all 1120 sets and directly tests the graph-geodesic criterion for a witness and all 120 possible extensions; infinite extrapolation is not used.

value.rationale: A published problem asks for lower total mutual-visibility in hypercubes, and optimal sets correspond to minimum independent dominating sets in the halved cube: canonical objects in visibility and coding theory. The seven-cube is the first small halved cube requiring four centers, offering a natural nontrivial finite cutoff. Complete equality-case rigidity and the exact labeled census supply information not contained in the known scalar domination number, and permit direct construction of all optima. The result is motivated by an existing named problem rather than an arbitrary restriction.
